Each realm will begin the war commanding a force of 15 soldiers (which will represent the amount of health points for your tribe). Each round, your realm will decide on three actions to either Attack, Defend, or Train. Actions Attack - You will roll a 2-5 die, where the number rolled will represent the damage you will do to the tribe (you still do 2-5 damage even if you have less than the amount of troops of the dice roll). Defend - Lets you block any attack successfully and captures an enemy troop. You may not select this action 2 turns in a row. Train - Gain +1 soldier (up to 20). If you get attacked, this action gets voided. Targeting Rules
  • You can only target one team per Attack.
  • If your chosen target is already eliminated, your attack fails that round.
  • When a realm’s soldiers are reduced to 0, they are eliminated from the war. At the end of every round, your realm will receive an update on your current troop.
I will also open up 1on1 tribal chat with the other tribes where you can talk to them about strategy. So, @Heralds please designate a War Commander who will basically be the one responsible for pinging me with your decision, they will have the final say with all your moves.

Not a bad moment, but do you mind if I add to it? They were someone bestowed some level of godly power as a reward for heroism, and at one point had a very “with great power comes great responsibility” mindset. And then that happens, and they suddenly feel ill-content with their measly responsibilities. “Only defending a small town? I should be defending cities, dammit! These people DIED, I’ve proven myself to be trustworthy, and these fatsos in the skies did nothing!” There grows a resentment towards the gods, and he tries his best to prove himself as worthy of more. The other gods refuse him though, as they see a level of immaturity. As he goes though, he reaches the limits of what his current powers can prove, and eventually starts trying to trick the gods. This fails, and he is punished by losing all physical power. They relent and give some back, but they place a curse on him so that what he faces will always be slightly stronger. No matter how powerful he gets, he’ll never be able to win until he learns to be content.

Agni was far from the only god in the pantheon who didn’t work for their power, whom he felt never experienced sufficient pain to deserve it. No, he was only a rung in a ladder. More was to come. And more was exactly what he wanted… or so he thinks. On that day, Phani, The God of Envy was born. Realizing he wouldn’t get anywhere without some help, he works to poison the minds of those misfortuned like him into believing that more was the answer. More power, more money, anything they want. As long as he could tempt them, he could trick them into joining his army… but only to fill his own pocket.
